national.title: After last year's storm, this remote Alaska town is still picking up the pieces
national.summary: In October, 2025, the remnants of a typhoon seriously damaged Alaska Native villages in the far western part of the state. A year later, one of the hardest hit communities is still recovering.
national.body:
Construction crews work on houses and other building throughout Kipnuk after ex-typhoon Halong hit Alaska's coast in October of 2025. Gabby Hiestand Salgado/KYUK hide caption

Last fall , the remnants of Typhoon Halong tore through numerous small Alaska Native villages off the road system in Western Alaska. The storm destroyed infrastructure, floated homes off their foundations, and displaced over a thousand people. A year later, hundreds remain displaced as the slow work of repair in a remote part of the state continues. And in one of the hardest hit communities – the small town of Kipnuk – people still aren't sure when they'll be moving back.

Environment What we know about the devastating storm in Western Alaska 'Working as fast as we can' The village of under 200 homes is situated on the wide open tundra and only consistently accessible by plane.

A year ago, 90% of the residences here were damaged by the remnants of Typhoon Halong, according to the State of Alaska's Emergency Operations Center. Dozens were swept off their foundations, some with families still inside . The community is now largely scattered across Alaska – some outside the region their ancestors have lived in for thousands of years.

Kipnuk 10 months after ex-typhoon Halong hit Alaska's coast in October of 2025. Gabby Hiestand Salgado/KYUK hide caption

Throughout the past year, crews have been working on repairs.

On a clear day in August, Eddie Chuckwuk's construction crew attempted what sounded like magic: raising a building back onto its foundations using air compressors.

Only on NPR Archaeologists are racing to save precious artifacts in Alaska after last year's storm Chuckwuk is one of several dozen people who have been working long days to rebuild the place where he grew up.

national.title: Can I trust the polls? And other questions from listeners about the 2026 midterms
national.summary: Ahead of Election Day, listeners send in questions about whether debates are dead, if polls are reliable for election coverage and how Trump might work with Democrats if they win control of Congress.
national.body:
Ahead of Election Day, there are a lot of questions about what might happen, what the implications of different outcomes might be and even what it's like to cover elections. In collaboration with the NPR Politics Podcast, listeners sent in their questions about the election and politics for our political correspondents to answer.

This is a common question every election cycle, but it's a little like saying, "I don't like the media because the media is biased." There are good polls and bad polls just like there are good reporters and bad reporters.

Elections Here are the Senate races to watch ahead of Election Day There have no doubt been some high-profile misses, particularly at the state level. National polls have actually been pretty good when it comes to the horse race, with a slight underestimation of Republican turnout. But remember, these polls have margins of error. That means a poll with +/- 3 or 4 percentage points is actually a range of 6 to 8 points. That's important because in a country with very close elections, the kind of precision that Americans expect sets up the polls for failure because they're not intended to be that specific. They set more of a fuzzy range.

State surveys have seen a lot of junk polls, even a couple fake ones this time around. So it's really important to pay attention to the quality of the pollster. The reason for this is because of the decline of local journalism. Local newspapers and TV stations just don't have the kind of money that national outlets do to pay for good, rigorous and frequent polling.

Horse-race polling isn't even the best use of polling. I talk a lot about polls, but you rarely hear me talking about specific margins between candidates, unless there's been a trend moving the needle in a certain direction. The races are close, within margin of error in many places, and that's all that really needs to be conveyed. Unfortunately, some outlets emphasize the horse race, but the best stuff is underneath. Are there trends over time with statistically significant movement on important questions and issues? For example, we wouldn't know how quickly public opinion moved on important issues, approval ratings, attitudes and how strongly people feel about those things without this data.

Only on NPR Democrats still poised to make gains, but poll shows warning signs for just how many Also, for those who don't think reporters should use polls at all, understand that campaigns and corporations spend millions of dollars on polling to inform where they spend money, where they travel and what messages to use. They use the same pollsters you hear about externally. All that said, polling is one tool. It's not everything, and it should be mixed with historical context, reporting with campaigns, and being on the ground, which are all priorities of NPR's as well. - Domenico Montanaro, NPR senior political editor and correspondent

national.title: Plans for a data center threaten scenic wilderness and dark skies in West Virginia
national.summary: Residents are fighting back against plans for a project that would span thousands of acres near the Monongahela National Forest and popular outdoor recreation, ski areas and dark sky sites.
national.body:
White Grass Ski Touring Center in Canaan Valley , W.Va., is celebrated for its unusually curvy and hilly cross-country skiing terrain. Chris Jackson for NPR hide caption

DAVIS, W.Va. — Stretching nearly a million acres through the rugged mountains of eastern West Virginia, the Monongahela National Forest links some of the state's best known natural attractions. The vast area ranges from the ski slopes of Canaan Valley to the dark skies of Blackwater Falls and Spruce Knob and includes the small towns of Davis and Thomas that serve as gateways for visitors to the region.

Climate Data centers are booming. But there are big energy and environmental risks For the past seven months, Kaleb Skelton, his wife, Ella, their 2-year-old son, Ryder, and dog Mabel have lived in a camper in this corner of West Virginia's "almost heaven." Kaleb is finishing a seasonal stint as a campground manager on a lake near Spruce Knob, the state's highest point.

On clear nights atop the isolated peak, they get to experience a river of stars in one of the very few pockets of darkness remaining in the Eastern United States. The area has become a draw for amateur astronomers.

Spruce Knob Lake Campground hosts Kaleb and Ella Skelton, at their site at Spruce Knob on Saturday, Oct. 10 2026 in Spruce Knob, W.Va. The couple from Texas have been at the site since April and said they have never seen darker skies than atop Spruce Knob. Chris Jackson for NPR hide caption

During summer's new moons, Kaleb says, one in four campsites he oversees is occupied by someone with a telescope. He thought his family's cabin in eastern Texas offered "the craziest" dark skies he'd ever seen, "but coming out here definitely rivals it."

Those inky-black nights — and the natural beauty they shelter — are now under threat from what many residents see as a modern-day version of extractive industries like logging and mining that once defined the region. In a place where tourism, outdoor recreation and community are deeply intertwined, a gigantic power plant and data center campus in nearby Tucker County would bring large-scale development into the heart of it all.

A stark image of the town of Davis from 1885, during the heyday of logging, is a reminder of that transformation. The photo shows a handful of squat buildings amid a broad clearing littered with forest remains.

national.title: Oil company earnings skyrocket — again
national.summary: Oil companies are reporting another quarter of sky-high profits as the war in Iran pushes up the price of oil — and prices at the pump.
national.body:
A pump jack operates at sunset in the Permian Basin near Loving, N.M., on Tuesday, May 20, 2025. Susan Montoya Bryan/AP hide caption

Oil companies made billions this quarter, they told investors on calls this week. ExxonMobil earned $15.4 billion, more than doubling its earnings compared to this time last year.

Together, the three companies pulled in just over $36 billion this quarter.

Middle East conflict Oil companies report sky-high profits thanks to wartime crude prices As with the soaring profits oil companies recorded last quarter , it's largely due to the war in Iran disrupting the global oil supply. Less oil is moving through the Middle East, so the oil in other parts of the world has become much more valuable.

Brent crude is now trading around $113 a barrel . For context, before the war began, it was about $70 a barrel.

Business Tariffs, diesel and computer chips are driving up costs for automakers Business The Trump administration weakens fuel efficiency standards for new cars Meanwhile, demand for oil and refined products like gasoline, diesel and heating oil hasn't changed much. People still need them to heat homes , drive cars, run tractors and truck everything we buy around the country.

Dan Pickering, founder of the financial services firm Pickering Energy Partners, says that big oil companies are profiting as they meet that demand. " The majors are able to sell their barrels that they produce in the U.S. or Latin America or Europe for much higher prices," he said. "So the Middle East's loss is generally the gain of oil and gas companies in the U.S. and Europe."

On their earnings calls, oil company executives said a good chunk of their profits were going to their shareholders through dividends and stock buybacks. Shell's buyback was one of their biggest ever. Exxon announced its highest-ever quarterly dividend.

national.title: Your writing was flagged as AI. What does that actually mean?
national.summary: As editors turn to imperfect AI detection tools to weed out machine-generated submissions, writers who say they were falsely accused of using AI are left wondering what triggered a positive result.
national.body:
Ghostwriter Sally McGraw was hoping to land a job developing a book proposal for a prospective client. But after submitting a writing sample, she got an unexpected response: an email telling her that multiple artificial intelligence detection tools had flagged her work as machine-generated.

"I was floored because I had not used AI to generate the text," McGraw said. "I'd written it all myself."

Having spent more than 20 years as a professional nonfiction writer, McGraw said she was angry that her work had been dismissed as AI-written.

"You know where you see a cartoon character going red from their chin all the way up to the crown of their head? I felt my ears starting to burn," she said. "I thought, what is going on?"

McGraw said she assured the client she had written the proposal herself, but decided not to press the issue because she considered the job "minor."

Sally McGraw, a ghostwriter, said she's changed her writing style after a prospective client suggested her work was AI-generated. Sally McGraw hide caption

In an email to NPR, the client confirmed that she had screened McGraw's work for AI. But she said the results were not the determining factor in choosing to hire a different writer, instead citing experience and fit. McGraw says she was paid for her writing samples, but believes the detector results cost her the opportunity to write the full book proposal.

As editors struggle to keep up with a growing influx of AI-generated content, some are turning to detection tools to help sift through the mounting number of submissions. But these tools aren't perfect: They've been known to falsely flag human-written work as AI, which can leave writers with little idea of what triggered the result and how to prove otherwise.

national.title: 100 years later, Harry Houdini's death still haunts Detroit
national.summary: The legacy of magician Harry Houdini still looms large in Detroit 100 years after his death there. Some mark the anniversary of Houdini's death by trying to make contact with his spirit.
national.body:
Escape artist Harry Houdini is shown before being lowered in a packing crate into the ice-covered Detroit River in 1907. AP Photo hide caption

This Halloween marks the 100th anniversary of the death of the legendary magician Harry Houdini.

He earned his reputation by freeing himself from traps that seemed impossible for a mere mortal to survive.But Houdini couldn't escape the ultimate fate waiting for him in Detroit on Oct. 31, 1926, and his spirit still haunts the Motor City.

Houdini performed in Detroit 19 times between the early days of his career in 1894 and the final show of his life in 1926.

The trajectory took him from being a bottom-of-the-bill act to one of the most famous entertainers in the world.

He escaped obscurity by declaring no set of handcuffs or jail cell could hold him. He dangled upside down from office buildings wearing a straitjacket, dramatically removing them in full view of those raptly watching below. Sometimes the buildings housed a local newspaper, ensuring free publicity for Houdini's upcoming stage shows.

In 1906, Houdini jumped two dozen feet from Detroit's Belle Isle Bridge into the frigid river below, bound with two sets of police handcuffs. He emerged unscathed, but the legend around it grew. The escape artist had leaped into a hole in ice covering the river, the story went, finding air pockets to breathe in before finally surfacing.

Reports from the time show the river was not actually frozen. But that didn't stop movies decades later from portraying it that way.

national.title: Daylight saving time is almost over. Here's what to know.
national.summary: Millions of Americans gain an hour of sleep this weekend when the time change commonly known as daylight savings ends for 2026, meaning clocks "fall back."
national.body: Millions of Americans will gain an hour of sleep this weekend when the twice-a-year time change commonly known as daylight savings ends for 2026. Most of the U.S. will "fall back" an hour when the clocks change at 2 a.m. on Sunday.Here's what to know about what's formally known as daylight saving time as it ends for the year:What is daylight saving time, and why do we have it?Daylight saving time is the period during the year, from March to early November, when the majority of the U.S. operates one hour ahead of standard time.The move effectively "saves" an hour of daylight from the morning and adds it to the evening during the spring and summer months when the days are the longest. In the fall and winter months, when the days are shorter, the U.S. returns to standard time, with daylight coming earlier in the morning.For example, in Boston on Saturday, before the time change, the sun will rise at 7:16 a.m. and set at 5:39 p.m., according to the National Weather Service. On Sunday, back on standard time, sunrise will be at 6:17 a.m. and sunset will be at 4:37 p.m.The U.S. first adopted daylight saving time in 1918 during World War I as an effort to conserve fuel after Europe implemented its own time change, according to the Congressional Research Service. After the war, Congress repealed the clock switch but gave states the option to continue observing it.During World War II and the 1970s energy crisis, Congress brought year-round daylight saving time to the U.S., again with the goal of reducing energy consumption. These experiments didn't last long.After the war, the U.S. let states and municipalities decide for themselves if they wanted to keep daylight saving time and when to observe it. (Congress didn't establish a uniform start and end for the time change until 1966.) In the '70s, continuous daylight saving time was stopped before reaching the 10-month mark.Will the U.S. move to year-round daylight saving time?Earlier this year, legislation to once again make daylight saving time last all year long cleared a major hurdle in Congress. The bill, called the Sunshine Protection Act, passed the House in July and went to the Senate. national.title: Hundreds evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky during rare Ukraine ceasefire
national.summary: Hundreds of people are also understood to have stayed in the front-line town, despite the dangers.
national.body:
Hundreds of residents of the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have been evacuated, Russian and Ukrainian authorities have said, following a humanitarian ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump.

"Everything unfolded without any incidents, and both sides noted the high level of organisation," Russia's human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova said.

Planes carrying Oleshky residents landed in the city of Gomel, Belarus on Saturday morning, Belarusian state media and a senior Ukrainian official said.

The evacuees are expected to board buses to drive across the border into Ukraine's Chernihiv region later on Saturday.

Speaking to journalists on Friday evening, Lantratova put out a joint request with her Ukrainian counterpart "to the US First Lady... that humanitarian missions such as this one, delivering aid to residents in need, be conducted on a regular basis under the coordination of Mrs Melania Trump".

Melania Trump said that "all elements of the convoy, including the safe passageway in and out of Oleshky, was established through mutual agreement between Russian and Ukrainian leaders".

A ceasefire - the longest and most widespread since the start of Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 - has been in force in the entire frontline region of Kherson since Tuesday, allowing for the road out of Oleshky to be demined.

Residents who wished to leave had a four-hour window to do so on Friday. A convoy of 25 buses was brought in to allow up to 750 people to leave the town until 14:00 (12:00 GMT), along with ambulances for people with limited mobility.

national.title: Trump predicts Iran war will end soon as Qatar pushes for a deal
national.summary: Trump predicts the war with Iran is "going to end soon," without offering any details, as Qatari mediators return to Tehran to push for a deal.
national.body: Saudi air defences intercepted a drone in the Riyadh region on Saturday, according to the spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis. "Air defences intercepted and destroyed a hostile drone in the Riyadh region," Turki al-Malki wrote on X, adding that "debris from the interception fell without causing injuries." Malki did not say who launched the drone. In recent weeks, Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis have ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, including by launching deadly strikes on Riyadh airport that forced its closure for two weeks and the cancellation of flagship events. On Friday, Malki said the Houthis had targeted the Medina region, home to Islam's second holiest city, but the group later denied the claim. The Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure, airports and ships come after hostilities resumed in Yemen over the summer between the Houthis and the country's internationally recognised government, which is backed by Riyadh. More than 1,600 people have been killed and over 275,000 displaced since the fighting reignited, according to United Nations figures. CBS/AFP

national.title: U.S. approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
national.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged his allies to speed up deliveries of the critical munition.
national.body: The State Department approved on Friday the sale of 500 Patriot missile defense systems to Ukraine at a cost $2.1 billion.In a statement released Friday, the State Department said the purchase will be paid for by Ukraine with donations from Canada and European allies such as Germany and Norway, and that no U.S. funds are involved in the sale."This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a partner country that is a force for political and economic stability in Europe," the department said. It also added the principal contractor in this agreement is Lockheed Martin and that there would be "no adverse impact" on U.S. defense readiness.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy lauded the decision, and thanked President Trump, but warned that it may take years for the munitions to be delivered to Ukraine. "We are asking our American partners to find a solution for the time when there is a real danger," Zelenskyy appealed on Friday evening.In a post on X, the Ukrainian president said there had been more than 30 Russian strikes on his country's energy infrastructure in the past two weeks, targeting "the systems that sustain life in our cities and communities."He appealed to the United States and European allies to provide Ukraine with the Patriot systems currently in their own stockpiles and replenish their arsenals with these 500 missiles, purchased by Ukraine, in the coming years."We are asking for decisions that can guarantee the protection of lives not the day after tomorrow or sometime later, but at the very moment the threat is there," Zelenskyy added.Ukraine has long warned of dwindling supplies of Patriots, which it uses to intercept strikes from Russia, and has previously accused the U.S. of slowing down deliveries of the critical missiles.The development comes amid ongoing tensions between Ukraine's president and Mr. Trump, who faced criticism for waiving new sanctions on Russia just days before they were expected to take effect.

national.title: Spain train disaster clouds Sánchez chances of re-election
national.summary: The Spanish PM is hit by a succession of crises just weeks before a snap general election.
national.body:
The breaking news from Spain this week was shocking but also shockingly familiar: another collision on the high-speed rail line south from Madrid, with reports of dozens killed.

It is just nine months since two trains crashed near Cordoba, killing 46 people. Now 69 bodies have been recovered here in central Spain, from wreckage strewn over the tracks and down an embankment.

For the victims' families it is devastating; a personal tragedy.

But it is also a national disaster that has shattered confidence in the country's rail network and the Socialist-led government of Pedro Sánchez. It is playing out just weeks before the snap general election he called.

The formal investigation into the Toledo train disaster has only just been launched but the government has been quick to take control of the narrative.

From the first hours after the collision, Transport Minister Oscar Puente began suggesting "human error" was to blame, batting responsibility as far as possible from the cabinet.

On Friday, he appeared before the press for a second time to set out what he called the "objective facts" of the crash and counter a surge of criticism against the government.

The opposition People's Party (PP) is among those calling for his resignation as a "moral" and "ethical" move.

national.title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader
national.summary: What does Joseph Kabila launching a new rebel movement mean for DR Congo?
national.body:
Joseph Kabila was a commander in the rebel alliance that brought his father to power in the Democratic Republic of Congo in 1997, went on to succeed him as president and now, at the age of 55, he is a rebel leader once again.

In an even stranger twist, the man he has sworn to topple is the very man he handed power to after 18 years at the helm, and with whom he had formed a coalition government after stepping down. While one of the rebel groups he had fought against as president is part of his new alliance.

His career reflects the ever-shifting nature of politics in DR Congo, where alliances are ephemeral, with the use of force a constant threat.

When Kabila was named leader of the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), earlier this month, it confirmed what many Congolese had long believed – that the former president was working with the M23 rebels, who last year seized much of eastern DR Congo, including the region's main cities of Goma and Bukavu.

Nevertheless, the confirmation sent shockwaves through DR Congo – a vast country two-thirds the size of western Europe, with huge deposits of gold, diamonds and even more importantly minerals used to make everything from the mobile phones to batteries for electric vehicles.

For Kabila, the alliance offers a possible route back to the power he had lost.

For the M23 rebels, his involvement brings the experience and networks of a former head of state to a movement whose military advances have yet to translate into broad national legitimacy.

But it is far from certain that they can achieve their stated goal of ousting President Félix Tshisekedi.

national.title: Trump's tariffs could shutter this Canadian town - its residents are fighting to save it
national.summary: A century-old paper mill in Témiscaming, Quebec is indefinitely closed after the US imposed 50% tariffs on its products, putting hundreds out of work.
national.body:
As you cross the Ottawa river into Témiscaming, Quebec, the paper mill takes up much of the horizon.

The town itself was built over a century ago, around the mill and the region's forests filled with pine, birch, spruce and fir. Now, the main employer and economic anchor sits idle after trade talks broke down between Canada and the US and President Donald Trump imposed more tariffs on the country.

Most of the mill‘s 360 employees are out of work, kept afloat for the moment with partial pay from government tariff-relief.

For some, like Nadine Suley, the shuttering of the mill could mark not just a lost livelihood, but a lost way of life.

She is not "a city girl", and is heading out moose hunting later to take advantage of the short season, like much of the town. She quips they'll all need the free meat provided by the animals this year.

"It's not just a job. It's our home," Suley says, adding that the US tariffs on her town feel like "a personal attack".

In early October, American owner RYAM went ahead with an "economic shutdown" of the mill for "an indefinite period".

Property values in Témiscaming fell almost overnight, and "For Sale" signs dot the yards of modest middle-class homes that make up most of the town.

national.title: Why North Korea's 'elite' hackers are the prime suspect in major Binance hack
national.summary: If the accusations are true, the record-making heist shows how powerful suspected North Korean hackers have become.
national.body:
Two major blockchain analytics firms say they have robust intelligence pointing to a North Korean state-backed group as the likely culprits in the $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack of Binance , the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange.

The Lazarus Group, a North Korean hacking unit also known as TraderTraitor, was identified "with high confidence" by TRM Labs, as well as Chainalysis.

This incident is just the latest linked to the country, one of the poorest in the world and where access to the internet is severely restricted.

Experts accuse the government of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un of relying on cybercrime to finance itself, something Pyongyang has long denied.

Though not financial, the nation's most spectacular suspected hack took place in 2014. The target: Sony Pictures, which had made the Hollywood film The Interview. The film involves a plot to assassinate Kim.

The resulting hack exposed thousands of embarrassing emails exchanged among the studio's top executives.

national.title: The Indian chef who brought curry to America - then vanished
national.summary: Indian chef Ranji Smile opened America’s first Indian restaurant in 1901 - then became a fake prince.
national.body:
One hundred and twenty-five years ago, in 1901, an Indian chef opened what was almost certainly the first Indian restaurant in the US.

Ranji Smile was one of the most colourful and enigmatic figures to shape the American food scene.

In the summer of 1899, Smile sailed from London to New York. We know hardly anything about his origins and early life, not even his real name.

"Ranji" was probably a nod to the Indian cricketing sensation KS Ranjitsinhji, then a star attraction at Test matches in Britain. "Smile" could have been an anglicisation of "Ismail".

Whatever his origins, Smile possessed an uncommon knack for reinvention. Once through the portals of Ellis Island, he appended a new name to his identity, something more in keeping with America's egalitarian promise: Joe.

Joe Ranji Smile arrived in New York to work at Sherry's Restaurant, a glittering new establishment on Fifth Avenue.

In London, he had been a curry cook at the Cecil and Savoy hotels. Here, according to an 1899 profile in Harper's, he was noticed by Sherry's owner, Louis Sherry, who invited him to bring his culinary skills across the Atlantic. Late Victorian London already boasted an Indian dining scene: as early as 1810, Sake Dean Mohamed, a native of Patna, had opened his Hindostanee Coffee House near Portman Square, plying customers with both curry and hookah.

Manhattanite tastebuds lacked much exposure to masala. There was, however, growing curiosity about India and its culture. Swami Vivekananda, the spellbinding orator and exponent of Hindu philosophy, enthralled audiences during his visits to the city in the 1890s. At the same time, more Indian sailors, students and professionals trickled into New York. This was probably why Louis Sherry decided to add a curry cook to his kitchen staff.

national.title: Responsible or panicked? Meet the people around the world already preparing for crisis
national.summary: Filter straws to a disposable toilet - people in the US, Japan, Sweden and Netherlands on what's in their emergency stashes.
national.body:
Sales of tinned food, radios and torches spiked in some shops after the UK government advised households what to stock up on in case of a national emergency.

While having this stash - or personal crisis kit - is new to the UK, it's common in many places across the world.

Countries facing extreme weather, natural disasters and fraught geopolitical situations regularly issue preparedness guidance - some even delivering booklets directly to homes.

So what do these emergency supplies look like for some and how do they manage it?

Thirty-year-old Andreas Wennerberg had never really thought about preparing for emergencies, until a government booklet arrived through his door two years ago.

Posted to every household in Sweden, it detailed what to stock up on and how to act "in case of crisis or war".

Andreas, who lives in Stockholm, built up a relatively small stockpile in his basement, including a crank radio, a tank with 10 litres of water and about €200 (£170) in cash. He says he already owned some of the items.

It was a "wake-up call", he says, but admits he hasn't followed the guidance in full.

national.title: Global nature talks reach deal but money remains an issue
national.summary: Countries have been trying to get a global agreement to halt nature decline back on track.
national.body:
In Armenia's capital this week a fight between politicians broke out - not the mass brawl in its parliament that was so widely documented on social media - but between delegates from nearly 200 countries.

The world's nations have been gathered in Yerevan for nearly two weeks negotiating, and arguing, over a new agreement on nature.

Early on Saturday morning, hours after talks were due to finish, they finally agreed the key parts of a new action plan.

"And that's it. Perfect," said the meeting president, Hambardzum Matevosyan.

Four years earlier the same countries had signed a landmark deal committing to "halt and reverse" the decline of nature.

That global deal in 2022 - the Global Biodiversity Framework - contained 24 targets including putting 30% of the world's land and seas into protection by the end of the decade.

The world is currently in a sixth mass extinction event with species becoming extinct at 100 times the natural rate because of human activities, scientists say.

But according to the UN this week, , external the world is on track to achieve just one of those two dozen targets.

national.title: Family of real estate CEO wounded in Toronto home invasion, officials say
national.summary: A search is underway for three armed men who broke into a mansion in Toronto, Canada, belonging to a real estate CEO in the early morning hours Thursday and attacked and injured the family inside, authorities said.
national.body: A search is underway for three armed men who broke into a mansion in Toronto, Canada, belonging to a real estate CEO in the early morning hours Thursday and attacked and injured the family inside, authorities said. The suspects, who were masked, forced their way through a back entrance of the five-bedroom home in the Bridle Path neighborhood at around 3:40 a.m. local time, wielding guns and a hammer, Toronto police said. Once inside, police said they went to the second floor of the home and confronted 75-year-old David Morton, his wife, 64-year-old Doriana Morton, and their two adult daughters, Maggie and Cristina. "There was a demand made for valuables from within the home," Toronto Police Service Inspector Kristy Smith told reporters. "Whether or not they escaped with anything is uncertain at this point." Police said David Morton, CEO of the MAC Group, and his daughters, ages 28 and 26, tried to fight off the intruders when shots were fired. All three sustained gunshot wounds, Smith disclosed. And in a separate statement Friday, David Morton said that all four family members were also attacked by the suspects with the hammer. David Morton said that he and his two daughters were still hospitalized Friday with gunshot wounds, but he did not provide details on their conditions. "What should have been the safety and security of our own home became a terrifying and life-threatening experience," David Morton said in his statement. "... It is difficult to put into words the trauma of experiencing something so horrific in the one place where everyone should feel safest: their own home." The three male suspects, all believed to be in their 20s and wearing dark clothing, fled the scene in an SUV, police said."All these houses have good security," Cecil Hawkins, a former resident of Bridle Path, said. "So I'm kind of surprised. Shooting people in the house, it just seems mind-boggling."According to Toronto police, there have been 119 home invasions so far in 2026, up 32.2% over this time last year.Thursday's home invasion happened in the same neighborhood where a mansion belonging to rapper Drake was targeted in multiple break-in attempts in May 2024. A security guard for Drake was also wounded in a shooting outside the home at that time.

national.title: Police deployed during stand-off over control of top Poland court
national.summary: The escalation came after the government suspended two senior justices and moved to bring criminal charges against them.
national.body:
Riot police have been deployed at Poland's Constitutional Court amid an escalating stand-off between the government and the court's top judges.

The row pits the government of Prime Minister Donald Tusk against his predecessors from the right-wing Law and Justice (PiS).

The police intervention came after Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek said he had requested stripping the court's President Bogdan Święczkowski and Vice-President Bartłomiej Sochański of their immunity from prosecution to bring criminal charges against them.

Tusk has vowed to depoliticise the judiciary, and on Friday defended the move as PiS supporters gathered outside the court premises in Warsaw in protest.

President Karol Nawrocki, who is backed by PiS, has now entered the constitutional court, according to his chief of staff.

Nawrocki cancelled a trip to Senegal mid-air in order to attend to the confrontation in Warsaw. He had been on his way to the Summer Youth Olympic Games in Dakar.

Riot police were deployed to prevent any demonstrators from entering the court building.

In a social media post, the Constitutional Court wrote that the two judges the government wants to prosecute were still the legally appointed senior justices of the court.

national.body: Anchorage, Alaska — The Justice Department's top prosecutor in Alaska said new reporting on the origins of an independent candidate's Senate campaign "has resulted in a significant surge of law enforcement assets" to the state, as federal officials in a separate civil case seek to segregate some of Alaska's Senate ballots.Michael Heyman, the U.S. attorney for the District of Alaska, called the allegations about how Daniel J. Sullivan — a man with the same first and last name as incumbent GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan — ended up on the ballot "troubling.""We are aware of the recent New York Times reporting regarding the Peltola campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, that they orchestrated a sprawling conspiracy to recruit and prop up Daniel J. Sullivan as a sham candidate, and we are taking that extremely seriously," he said in a press conference in Anchorage.But Heyman declined to detail what specific crimes are being investigated, saying he's "not making any assumptions on whether a crime has been committed or not.""That's what we do, is we investigate whether a crime has been committed under several theories, so I'm not going to comment on what those theories are, and I'm also not going to put the cart before the horse," he said.Asked by CBS News why the Justice Department is choosing to escalate the case ahead of the election, Heyman said, "We're not escalating anything except to the extent that a new article came out." "This has been going on sort of quietly for several months, with the intent not to escalate anything," he said, adding that investigators are going to take allegations involving election integrity seriously, even if a few days before the election. national.summary: The incumbent Republican running for re-election and allies have accused the Democrats of trying to confuse voters by recruiting a second Dan Sullivan to also stand in the race.
national.body:
Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola has denied she knew anything about an alleged "scheme" that led to two men named Dan Sullivan standing in the Alaska Senate race.

The denial comes as the Trump administration continues to escalate a criminal investigation into the matter, including a request for election officials to separate ballots that rank retired teacher Dan J Sullivan.

Senator Dan S Sullivan, the incumbent Republican running for re-election, and allies have accused the Democrats of trying to confuse voters.

The Alaska race is considered by analysts to be one of the tightest in the upcoming US midterm elections, which will decide which party controls Congress.

"I just want to clear the air," Peltola said while speaking to voters on Thursday. "I knew nothing about any other candidate on the ballot except for me and the incumbent. That is all I have ever known about. I am not interested in tricking voters."

Alaska's Republican Governor Mike Dunleavy ordered an official inquiry earlier this week into the alleged scheme.

Heyman did not immediately provide details of specific crimes his office would investigate.

Both Dan Sullivans have been running for the open Senate seat for some time. Still, controversy erupted earlier this week when The New York Times , external reported that Peltola's team worked with people who tried to recruit spoiler candidates in the Senate race.

national.summary: Stevens has demanded El-Sayed condemn an outside group's ad and apologize for comments he made about Israel. El-Sayed said Stevens is "intent on relitigating" their primary.
national.body: Washington â Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and his Democratic primary rival, Rep. Haley Stevens, clashed Friday ahead of a Sunday campaign event where both were expected to make a rare appearance together.The public rift between the two Democrats comes just days before one of the country's most hotly contested Senate races, as Republican nominee Mike Rogers seeks to peel off centrist Democratic voters. El-Sayed and the more moderate Stevens offered starkly differing visions for the future of the party during the primary, and although Stevens endorsed El-Sayed after he won the nomination, the two largely haven't campaigned alongside each other.In a statement Friday evening, El-Sayed said Stevens "seems intent on relitigating a primary that ended three months ago." The dig came hours after Stevens demanded that El-Sayed â a vehement critic of U.S. aid to Israel â apologize for suggesting during the campaign that "Israel is the reason Michigan cannot afford schools, health care, and child care." "Abdul promises to get money out of politics," Stevens said in the statement. "He can begin by getting Israel out of his explanation for everything Michigan cannot afford."She also urged El-Sayed to condemn an ad from an outside PAC that she said was antisemitic. national.body:
As Americans prepare to vote in the US midterm elections, candidates with their eye on Congress are not just competing on policy.

In our social media age, they're using their personal style to attract attention and project their message. Their clothing has become a measure of their authenticity and appeal.

"Politicians are dressing for two jobs at once: to look capable of holding office but to also look connected to the people they want to represent," said Joe Zee, a celebrity fashion stylist.

From Alaska to Texas, here is a look at how some candidates have been standing out on the campaign trail.

Some candidates, like Democrat Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, who represents Washington's 3rd Congressional District, are embracing a relaxed, outdoorsy image.

The former car repair shop owner is up for re-election on a platform focused on support for small businesses and working families, after capturing a Republican-held seat in her state in 2022.

She favours low fuss, low-key work jackets, flannel shirts, jeans and practical footwear.

Robert Ordway, conservative public policy adviser and former owner of Capitol Hill Clothiers, says Gluesenkamp Perez is probably the most "spot-on" when it comes to "authenticity and where you come from".

national.title: For many, striped bass fishing is a way of life. But the iconic species could face collapse
national.summary: Scientists who study striped bass say anglers on the East Coast are right to be concerned, and they say years of overfishing are just part of the problem.
national.body:
Patrick Whittle, Associated Press Patrick Whittle, Associated Press

Robert F. Bukaty, Associated Press Robert F. Bukaty, Associated Press

MONTAUK, N.Y. (AP) — Striped bass fishing has been Bill Jakob's passion for more than 60 years, and he remembers an era when he'd spend all night casting his line into the crashing waves off Montauk and get eight or nine fish ranging up to 40 pounds (18 kilograms), a big catch by anyone's standards.

Then, after years of heavy fishing, the big runs of stripers stopped.

WATCH: Montanans fish for answers to mysterious decline in trout population

"I'm part of the problem, back in the years. I ran party boats, we slayed fish with reckless abandon," said Jakob, president of the Montauk Surfcasters Association on the easternmost tip of Long Island.

Increasingly, fishermen like Jakob fear the good days of catching striped bass are coming to an end. The fish aren't showing up like they used to, and young stripers are becoming harder to find.

Scientists who study striped bass say anglers on the East Coast are right to be concerned, and they say years of overfishing are just part of the problem. The fish have experienced eight consecutive years of poor reproduction in their most critical habitat in the Chesapeake Bay, regulators said last week, and the population has declined along much of the Atlantic coast.

local.title: Domestic violence case handling changes in imperfect system
local.summary: More often than not, when it comes to domestic violence cases in court, victims find it hard to navigate the system or to get themselves heard. Attorney Sally Jaroszynski has been practicing law for over 30 years, and in that time she said things have changed when it comes to domestic violence cases
local.body:
More often than not, when it comes to domestic violence cases in court, victims find it hard to navigate the system or to get themselves heard.

Attorney Sally Jaroszynski has been practicing law for over 30 years, and in that time she said things have changed when it comes to domestic violence cases, and while things remain difficult to navigate there is also help for victims out there.

The way cases were handled in 1993, Jaroszynski said, when she first began versus how domestic violence cases are handled now is very different.

"I think the courts have made some strides in how they handle domestic violence cases, but it's tricky and difficult to navigate sometimes," Jaroszynski said. "When I started practicing in '93 we didn't have an Integrated Domestic Violence Court."

Something else that is different these days, Jaroszynski said, is that there is the ability with the IDV Court for one judge to hear multiple different aspects or proceedings in connection to the case, as that judge presides over all of them, even with them being separate proceedings. Chautauqua County has that in IDV court with Judge Stephen Cass, who Jaroszynski said does a wonderful job as he is very well trained in domestic violence. But, she added, if a case does not get pulled into IDV court, that is when people can get lost and struggles can begin.

"It's hard when you're not trained in domestic violence as extensively as maybe our IDV judges are, because I think the difficulty is that people believe just a couple of incidents of physical violence is what is considered domestic violence," Jaroszynski said. "Domestic violence is so much more difficult to prove than sometimes physical violence."

Other areas of domestic violence that Jaroszynski said are more difficult to prove include coercive control, or restricting a partner's freedom or activities. Other forms of abuse take the forms of psychological abuse, economic abuse, stalking or harassment, and one that Jaroszynski said they see even more often today, and never saw when she first started, is through technology and social media.

"All of those issues together are things that pop up in domestic violence that I've had several clients who I sit with and counsel for the first time, and they have no idea that the technology abuse and the stalking and harassment and the economic and psychological abuse and coercive control, they don't even recognize that that's domestic violence," Jaroszynski said. "If they don't recognize it, you better hope that the judge does. And sometimes, it's really hard to prove."

local.body:
The family of a Jamestown man killed in a wrong-way crash in 2023 on Interstate 86 is refiling its case in state Supreme Court after the original 2025 filing was dismissed due to a procedural error.

Sandra Town, Joseph Town and the estate of Todd A. Town refiled their suit in state Supreme Court earlier this week after the 2025 case was dismissed because of an issue with the way the lawsuit was served upon Werner Enterprises Inc. and Brandon D. Cox. The lawsuit seeks compensatory damages for the wrongful death of Todd A. Town, compensatory damages for injuries and losses sustained by Sandra Town and Todd Town before he died, funeral expenses, damages arising from pre-impact physical pain and suffering, mental terror and mental anguish of the Towns.

A lawsuit filed in 2025 was dismissed on May 6 by state Supreme Court Justice Grace Hanlon, who granted a motion to dismiss because the lawsuit had not been properly filed upon Werner and Cox.

State law allows plaintiffs to file a new action in certain circumstances within six months of a similar filing being dismissed. That time period ends on Nov. 5, 2026, attorney Andrew Debbins wrote in his affirmation in support of an Order to Show Cause filed this week in state Supreme Court in Mayville. Debbins is asking the court to allow the filing to be served upon Joel B. Schechter, a Buffalo attorney who represented Werner Enterprises in the original lawsuit. Personally serving Cox would be difficult in nine days since the truck driver is often

"The plaintiffs respectfully ask that this court order that service upon Mr. Schechter, including by email, be deemed good and sufficient service upon the defendants," Debbins wrote. "Service by other means within the required timeframe is impracticable."

The accident happened Jan. 28, 2023, when two people, one of whom was driving the wrong way in the westbound lane of Interstate 86 between the Strunk Road and North Main Street Extension exits.

According to the New York State Police, the agency handling the investigation, a driver in a 2009 Toyota Camry traveling east struck a westbound 2019 Ram 1500. The Ram was then hit from behind by a 2020 Freightliner.

The operator of the vehicle traveling in the wrong direction, later identified as Mathew A. Berry of Randolph, was pronounced dead at the scene. Police said Berry had been reported missing earlier in the day. There were two occupants in the Ram that was traveling west; one of the occupants, identified as Jamestown resident Todd A. Town, 57, was later pronounced dead while the other, Sandra L. Town, 54, suffered serious injuries and was transported by helicopter to UPMC Hamot in Erie, Pa.

local.body:
MILWAUKEE -- It was only fitting that the Milwaukee Brewers celebrated their first World Series title with a beer-soaked celebration worthy of their name.

“We’ve had way too many parade beers,” team captain and designated hitter Christian Yelich said Friday at a rally that capped a daylong party with fans. “I took the trophy to the face, got a black eye. It’s all worth it. It’s for you guys. We should celebrate forever.”

The small-market Brewers gave their long-suffering fans the championship they had been waiting for with a 4-1 win over the Tampa Bay Rays on Wednesday, clinching the Series in five games. It was their first time playing in the Fall Classic in 44 years.

“Unbelievable,” said parade attendee Mark Diedrich, a 76-year-old from who has been an on-and-off partial season ticket holder since the 1980s. “You just never thought it would happen. But it did.”

Before the rally at American Family Insurance Amphitheater near the shore of Lake Michigan, the Brewers held a parade through downtown Milwaukee. Exuberant fans flooded the streets, watched from parking garages and cheered from office building windows.

Milwaukee police estimated that over 750,000 attended the parade or rally, well above their initial expectations of about 400,000.

“That was incredible -- incredible,” manager Pat Murphy said. “I kept thinking I saw the same people over and over, and we were just going in a circle. There’s no way there’s that many people who live here.”

Then came a rally that featured World Series MVP William Contreras joining in on the fans’ “MVP” chants.

A recent Facebook post highlighted a need in the Dunkirk community that stretches far beyond just the city itself.

The Chautauqua County Rural Ministry shared that it is "facing a critical food shortage". The shelves of its food pantry were nearly empty as a plea went out to the area to help.

In the days that followed, the community responded tremendously.

"We're fortunate that people want to help us. The response has been incredible," said Bridget Majka, Executive Director of the Chautauqua County Rural Ministry. "The amount of people who have stopped in or have called us to see what we need, I've never seen anything like it, honestly, these past couple days. It's been amazing."

While the community came through in the moment, the issue is anything but solved.

This past week, the Rural Ministry's food pantry shelves were nearly barren because of the increased demand for assistance. In just one day, 40 families were fed through the food pantry, 20 new people came for lunch in person, 120 lunches were provided, and 100 takeout dinners were distributed.

"We have some hard days around here, and we have people that come in here and have very hard days. It's wonderful to know that there's other people out there that support us," Majka said. "It makes all the difference."

Majka said over the past 10 months to roughly a year, the Rural Ministry has seen an increase of about 30% in people who are utilizing their food programs.

local.body: As energy costs continue to put pressure on household budgets, Western New Yorkers are preparing for another winter of heating their homes.But how much will it cost to stay warm this year? local.title: Outcome of the Fairport mayoral election could take time
local.summary: How close the vote is likely will determine the level of priority given to sorting through write-ins.
local.body:
Voters in Fairport might have to wait some time before they know the outcome of the mayoral race there.

That's because while Deputy Mayor Heidi Woika is the only name on the ballot in Tuesday's general election , Village Trustee Tracy Briggs has mounted a formidable write-in campaign after narrowly losing the Democratic primary.

Election Night results will include vote tallies for Woika and a general category for write-ins, which could be Briggs or any name a voter chooses. Those will be reviewed after the election by a bipartisan team that will tabulate totals and assess how to count write-in votes with misspellings or partial names.

How close the two vote tallies are likely will determine the level of priority given to sorting through those write-ins to determine — in a matter of days, or weeks — how many get counted for Briggs.

"She worked hard in the off-season, and over the course of the last six years, she has just really blossomed."Now a team captain, MacKinnon leads by example in the pool and encourages her teammates as they work toward their own goals.WATCH: First Student Super 7 Athlete: Kenmore East's Amelia MacKinnonBourke said her determination stands out, especially when she faces a tough race. entertainment.title: Macklemore Wraps Up Free Palestine Tour in London: “It Was More Uncomfortable for Me to Stay Silent”
entertainment.summary: The concerts, raising money for Palestinian causes, come weeks after Macklemore was controversially dropped from Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour.
entertainment.body:
Macklemore brought the final night of his Free Palestine Tour to London on Friday, telling a U.K. audience: “I don’t believe that staying silent is brave.”

The sold-out event at the capital’s OVO Arena Wembley boasted a crowd of over 12,500 people, who cheered and screamed as U.S. rapper spoke.

The gigs come weeks after he was removed from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour for expressing his pro-Palestine views on stage. Sheeran later said it was a promoter decision to drop Macklemore, and that venues set to host the concerts threatened to pull out if Macklemore was on the bill. Related Stories Movies 'Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting' Review: Whimsical Chinese Film Explores Myth and History Through a Series of Tasty Treats Business Japan's Anime Industry Hits a Record High of $28 Billion in 2025

In response, Macklemore launched his own benefit concert with acts in the British capital such as Aja Monet, Cure for Paranoia, Dana Saleh, Nemahsis, Lucas Jones, Paloma Faith, Roze, Shadia Mansour and Vic Mensa. Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg was among the guest speakers, along with Hollywood superstars Mark Ruffalo, Susan Sarandon, Javier Bardem, Cynthia Nixon, as well as Melissa Barrera and Julian Casablancas, dialling in remotely.

“It was more uncomfortable for me to stay silent than to say something,” said Macklemore about the situation with Sheeran. “And I just want to say, I don’t believe that saying something is brave. I don’t believe that saying something is courageous. I believe that saying something is human. And those children in Gaza are our children. There is no separation.”

He continued: “I want to say thank you to every single soul that is in here tonight who decided to step up, leave their couch, be in community, be reminded and feel what that frequency of love feels like.” Macklemore added about the 50 members of the British House of Lords who urged the U.K. government to ban his concert: “Regardless of what the 50 Lords have to say, this is a story of equality for all human beings around this earth.”

All proceeds from the concerts in Dublin, Paris and London will go toward organizations supporting Palestinian communities through humanitarian relief, medical care, education, advocacy, policy change and community initiatives, according to the rapper’s team. Popular Irish acts Hozier and Kneecap were included on the lineup in Dublin , as was Boega, Sheeran’s backing band that pulled out of the Loop Tour in solidarity with Macklemore.

entertainment.title: Harry Styles Revives His ‘X Factor’ Audition Look for ‘Isn’t She Lovely’ at Harryween
entertainment.summary: The singer recreated his 2010 audition look for the Stevie Wonder cover at Madison Square Garden, the penultimate night of his 30-show residency.
entertainment.body:
Harry Styles went back to where it all started for Harryween.

At Madison Square Garden on Friday (Oct. 30), the 29th night of his 30-show Together, Together residency, Styles changed into the outfit he wore for his 2010 X Factor audition and performed Stevie Wonder ’s “Isn’t She Lovely,” the song that got him through to the next round at 16. He even repeated a line from that day, telling the crowd, “I work in a bakery,” a nod to the part-time job he held in his Cheshire hometown of Holmes Chapel.

The audition outfit was a mid-show swap. Styles opened the night dressed as Elvis Presley , while his band and dancers came as different versions of Styles from across his career. The Elvis nod tracks: the first song Styles ever recorded was a cover of Presley’s “The Girl of My Best Friend.” Related Morgan Wallen 'Now' Has Another Record on Billboard's Country Airplay Chart Aaron Frazer Doubles Down on Soul with New 'Corners' EP: 'Simple Things Can Be Elegant' Mizuho Kusanagi's 'Akatsuki no Yona' Vol. 48 Debuts at No. 1 on Billboard Japan Book Hot 100 Explore Harry Styles One Direction Stevie Wonder See latest videos, charts and news

On the audition itself, “Isn’t She Lovely” wasn’t Styles’ first pick. Footage released by the show in 2022 revealed he opened with Train ’s “Hey, Soul Sister,” and only sang the Wonder song a cappella after Simon Cowell asked to hear him without a backing track. He was later placed in One Direction alongside Niall Horan , Louis Tomlinson , Zayn Malik and the late Liam Payne . Earlier this month, Styles debuted “What Is Enough,” a song written for Payne, at the same venue on the second anniversary of Payne’s death.

Costumed covers have become a Harryween tradition. At the first edition, at MSG in 2021, Styles dressed as Dorothy to sing “Over the Rainbow,” then came out as a clown the next night to cover Britney Spears ’ “Toxic.” In 2022, at Los Angeles’ Kia Forum, he dressed as Grease ’s Danny Zuko for “Hopelessly Devoted to You.”

The residency wraps Saturday (Oct. 31) with a final Harryween show. The MSG run drew a record 11.5 million presale registrations on Ticketmaster. Styles has sent all four of his solo albums to No. 1 on the Billboard 200, most recently Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally. in March, and has topped the Hot 100 three times: “Watermelon Sugar” in 2020, “As It Was” in 2022 (15 weeks at No. 1, the longest run atop the chart by a U.K. act) and “Aperture” this year.

entertainment.title: Tame Impala Take On Seal’s ‘Kiss From a Rose’ for Like A Version
entertainment.summary: Kevin Parker said the ‘Batman Forever’ soundtrack was the first CD he ever bought; the band also played a stripped-back “Dracula”
entertainment.body:
Tame Impala got into the Halloween spirit a day early, covering Seal ’s “Kiss From a Rose” for Australian radio station triple j’s Like A Version series on Friday (Oct. 30). Explore Seal Tame Impala See latest videos, charts and news

At triple j’s Sydney studios, the band reworked the 1994 ballad into a stripped-back, synth-driven take, then followed it with a pared-down version of their own hit “Dracula.” Related Morgan Wallen 'Now' Has Another Record on Billboard's Country Airplay Chart Aaron Frazer Doubles Down on Soul with New 'Corners' EP: 'Simple Things Can Be Elegant' Mizuho Kusanagi's 'Akatsuki no Yona' Vol. 48 Debuts at No. 1 on Billboard Japan Book Hot 100

For Kevin Parker, the cover was a trip back to the start. He explained that “Kiss From a Rose” was on the first CD he ever bought, the Batman Forever soundtrack, which also introduced him to acts including U2, the Flaming Lips and Nick Cave.

It’s Tame Impala’s fourth Like A Version cover, following OutKast’s “Prototype” in 2013, Kylie Minogue’s “Confide in Me” in 2015 and Edwyn Collins’ “A Girl Like You” in 2021.

The session caps the biggest year of the project’s career. “Dracula,” first released as a solo single in October 2025, took off after a February remix featuring Jennie , giving Tame Impala their first top 10 on the Billboard Hot 100 with a No. 5 peak. The song also reached No. 1 on Pop Airplay and Hot Rock & Alternative Songs, and spent more than six months atop Hot Dance/Electronic Songs. Tame Impala have just come off their biggest Australian tour to date, and their album Deadbeat leads next month’s ARIA Awards with eight nominations, tied with Genesis Owusu.

Tame Impala recently wrapped the Australian leg of their Deadbeat Tour, which featured multiple arena shows in Brisbane, Melbourne and Sydney before finishing with two hometown performances in Perth on Oct. 24 and 25. Parker and his band are set to return to the road in May 2027 for a string of UK and European arena dates, followed by several summer festival appearances.

Seal’s original topped the Billboard Hot 100 for a week in August 1995 after its Batman Forever placement and won three Grammys the following year, including record and song of the year.

entertainment.title: 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards: ‘General Hospital’ Wins Best Daytime Drama
entertainment.summary: 'The Kelly Clarkson Show' won a leading five awards, as 'Beyond the Gates' also took home four trophies.
entertainment.body:
The 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards were presented Friday night, with General Hospital taking home the top prize of best daytime drama.

The series, which went into Friday night’s show up for 13 awards, won three other awards and saw its Genie Francis receive the lifetime achievement award. Beyond the Gates also won four awards, with star Tamara Tunie winning best actress in a daytime drama series. Best actor in a daytime drama went to The Bold and the Beautiful ‘s Scott Clifton.

Tunie, who won her first Daytime Emmy, paid tribute to the “host of Black actresses who paved the way for me, and I feel them as I stand here tonight, beginning with the legendary Cicely Tyson, the first Black woman to appear on a daytime television show, The Guiding Light .” Related Stories TV The Hollywood Reporter Wins 2026 Daytime Emmy Award Music Tom Morello, Annie Lennox, 'KPop Demon Hunters' Songwriters Honored at 2026 SONA Awards

Fellow best actress nominee Heather Tom, from The Bold and the Beautiful , was eyeing a record-setting seventh trophy, which would have made her the most awarded actress in daytime history.

The Young and the Restless led this year’s nominees with 18 nominations. Though it only won three awards, two of those came in the supporting performer categories. Roger Howarth was named best supporting actor, and Beth Maitland was named best supporting actress.

The Kelly Clarkson Show won five awards, including best daytime talk series, but the singer-host of the now-completed talk show didn’t appear to be at the Daytime Emmys . And Clarkson didn’t win the award for best daytime talk series host. Instead that honor went to fellow former talk show host Sherri Shepherd, whose eponymous talk show was canceled after four seasons.

Other notable winners include Tracee Ellis Ross, who won best travel and adventure program for her Solo Traveling show; Keke Palmer, who won for her work executive producing Glam Through the Ages ; and Ina Garten, who won best culinary host for her Be My Guest Food Network series, which was named best culinary instructional series.

Midway through the ceremony, NATAS chair Terry O’Reilly offered a timely, political speech, just days ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. Speaking about a congressman who was jailed in 1798 after criticizing the president in print, O’Reilly highlighed the power of the people.

entertainment.title: Kelly Clarkson Wins One & Loses One at 2026 Daytime Emmys
entertainment.summary: “Birdgate” had no bearing on the outcome. Voting concluded months ago.
entertainment.body:
The Kelly Clarkson Show won outstanding daytime talk series at the 2026 Daytime Emmys on Friday (Oct. 30), though its star, Kelly Clarkson , lost outstanding daytime talk series host to Sherri Shepherd for Sherri .

Clarkson won in one or both of those categories in six of the show’s seven seasons on the air. She has won a total of nine Daytime Emmys in seven years – five in the talk series category and four for talk series host – compared to three Grammys in a recording career which has lasted more than 20 years. Clarkson wasn’t present at the ceremony, which was held at the Hollywood Palladium for the first time.

Clarkson recently made headlines for an incident at a curiosity shop in Brooklyn where she maintained that she was treated poorly. But “Birdgate” had no bearing on the outcome here. There is just one round of Daytime Emmy voting, which determines both the nominations and the eventual winner. That round closed on June 10, four months before the incident.

The Kelly Clarkson Show won three other awards this year – best directing for a daytime studio non-fiction series; outstanding sound mixing and sound editing for a live daytime program; and outstanding art direction/set decoration/scenic design for a daytime program.

Ray Chew won outstanding music direction and composition for a daytime program for Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade . His award was accepted by his wife, who explained that he was busy working on Dancing With the Stars . Chew has also served in music direction capacities on American Idol, Saturday Night Live, the Emmy Awards, the BET Awards and the Grammy Awards’ Premiere Ceremony.

Keke Palmer won her first Daytime Emmy – outstanding daytime short form program as producer of Glam Through the Ages . Palmer has won two Primetime Emmys, for Keke Palmer’s Turnt Up With the Taylors and the reboot of Password .

Tracee Ellis Ross won outstanding travel and adventure program for Solo Traveling With Tracee Ellis Ross . It’s her first Emmy Award (Daytime or Primetime) following six Primetime Emmy nods for ABC’s blackish . Ross’ legendary mom, Diana Ross , has yet to win an Emmy.

Off Script With The Hollywood Reporter won outstanding arts and popular culture program, beating a pair of programs produced by their sister brand, Variety – Variety & CNN Actors on Actors and Variety Studio: Actors on Actors .

entertainment.title: Bill Maher Responds to Trump’s 1,318-Word Social Rant: “He Went Off on Me Like Kelly Clarkson in a Toy Store”
entertainment.summary: The president slammed the TV host in a Sunday post, writing that he is a "COMPLETE AND TOTAL LOSER."
entertainment.body:
Logo text Bill Maher has responded to President Donald Trump ‘s lengthy social media post where he slammed him as a “complete and total loser,” and shared more details about their recent dinner at the White House.

During Friday’s episode of Real Time with Bill Maher , the comedian addressed a few of the statements made in Trump’s post. He began the monologue by discussing the upcoming midterms and how former President Barack Obama caused a “big scandal” for a comment he made at a campaign rally saying that Trump has “got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.” Related Stories Music Canadian Rock Icon Bryan Adams Takes Aim at Trump, Says His Protest Song Gets Standing Ovations in Red States (Exclusive) Music Bryan Adams Releases New Trump Protest Song "Lake Ontario"

Maher said, “And the Republicans all said, ‘Leave the Cheesecake Factory out of this!’ Well, I mean, I should know. I just had dinner there. I hear it went well. What have you heard?”

The host then asked, “Now, did you see the 1,300-word Tweet he sent out? Longest ever. Kind of a flex.” He joked that “dining at the White House is the opposite of the Cheesecake Factory. After you leave, they review you.”

“He went off on me like Kelly Clarkson in a toy store,” Maher added. “I mean, eating with Trump is like dating Taylor Swift. It’s a lot of laughs at the time, but later on, they’re tearing you a new asshole.”

Maher was then handed a printed copy of Trump’s Truth Social post, and began to “address a few of the allegations.” Before that, he noted, “Look, I don’t want it to be this way. The whole point of having these dinners was talk, disagree, but listen, which he does in person, but don’t hate each other. And then I go back to my job here and then the heartaches begin.”

“It begins, ‘Let’s talk about the complete and total loser Bill Maher.’ You got me there. I’ll own that,” Maher joked, going on to explain “what pisses me off” is that “he doesn’t even notice what I say,” specifically citing a line in Trump’s post where he wrote, “[Maher] doesn’t think it was a good thing to take the Nuclear Weapon away from Iran, which shows you that he is not very smart.” Real Time then played a series of clips showcasing the opposite of Trump’s claim.

Maher then moved on to another section: “Page two, he talks about how I call him incessantly. I’ve never called you, you call me. I’d be afraid to call you. You’re the president. entertainment.title: LAPD Arrests Two for Murder of Christina Downer, Sister to ‘SNL’ Writer Jimmy Fowlie
entertainment.summary: Police arrested Downer's boyfriend, Delorean Bijon Brandon, and Kaylee Nicole Markowski on Thursday.
entertainment.body:
Two people have been arrested for the murder of Christina Downer, the sister to Saturday Night Live writer Jimmy Fowlie, the Los Angeles Police Department announced Friday.

Police arrested Downer’s boyfriend, Delorean Bijon Brandon, and Kaylee Nicole Markowski on Thursday.

“On December 18, 2025, Christina Downer was reported missing after her ex-husband requested a welfare check when he had not heard from her for an extended period of time. Downer’s boyfriend, Delorean Brandon, claimed that she had moved out several months earlier, leaving behind all her belongings, including her vehicle and dog,” the LAPD said. Related Stories Movies 'Fair Play' Doc About Olympic Gymnast Jordan Chiles Set for 2027 Release on Hulu, Disney+ (Exclusive) Movies Bill Hader Is the Cat in the Hat -- This Time a "Much Different Version" Than He Played on 'SNL'

In their statement, police said, “Robbery- Homicide Division detectives assumed the investigation after Downer’s cellphone was discovered washed ashore on Santa Monica Beach. Through various investigative techniques, detectives identified Delorean Brandon and Kaylee Markowski as the individuals responsible for Downer’s murder, the disposal of her body, and the concealment of their involvement.”

On Dec. 22, 2025, Fowlie shared a social media post asking for help finding his missing sister, sharing a multiple of images of Downer. Months later, in April of this year, he announced that “the LAPD has informed our family that Christina is no longer alive, and the case has officially transitioned from a missing person to a homicide investigation.”

The SNL writer shared in his April post that he believes his sister’s “phone and social media were compromised” in the weeks before she went missing, and those who took her phone “used it to hide the fact she was gone, to ask for money, and to create a false narrative that she was going ‘off the grid.’”

“I am sharing this because I believe that whoever is responsible is hoping to erase her in every way possible,” he wrote. “I want to amplify her story in the only way I know how. And to express that she was a beautiful person who matters in this world, especially to me.”

The LAPD’s Robbery-Homicide Division will present the case to the L.A. Country District Attorney’s Office for filing consideration. The investigation is still ongoing.

entertainment.title: ‘Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting’ Review: Whimsical Chinese Film Explores Myth and History Through a Series of Tasty Treats
entertainment.summary: In Qiu Jiongjiong's latest, highly stylized sets and costumes contribute to a strange banquet of storytelling where food plays a key role.
entertainment.body:
Following up his well-received 2021 feature A New Old Play , Sichuan-reared Chinese writer-director Qiu Jiongjiong continues to deploy heightened artifice and quasi-theatrical mannerisms (painted stage sets, rippling cloths representing water, actors in wacky costumes playing astral bodies or dogs, and so on) with his eccentric but addictive latest, Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting .

Although Fuxi runs a trim 135 minutes compared to New Old Play ’s three-hour run time, Qiu still manages to cover more than 2,000 years of myth, history and mythic history with a quartet of stories that revolve around special meals and banquets. (The word “fuxi,” intertitles helpfully explain, can either be a noun meaning delicious food or a verb signifying the savoring of such delicacies.) Related Stories Movies Eric Bauza Remembered as a "Once-in-a-Generation" Talent Who Gave Looney Tunes a New Voice Music Canadian Rock Icon Bryan Adams Takes Aim at Trump, Says His Protest Song Gets Standing Ovations in Red States (Exclusive) Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting The Bottom Line Spicy and addictive, if not easily digestible. Venue: Tokyo Film Festival (Competition) Cast: Lee Kang Sheng, Lee Hong-Chi, Annie Chen, Fan Guang Yao, Wang Talu, Wang Yitong, Xue Xuchun, Wang Hai, Zhou Jiarui Director/screenwriter: Qiu Jiongjiong 2 hours 15 minutes

The different segments, each one offering varying mixtures of slapstick comedy and memento mori solemnity, don’t have much to do with one another story-wise. So Qiu pulls it all together with a framing device about a film crew making each segment, the tales linked by the presence of the sun or Sol (Wen Ke) and Luna aka the moon (Xiao Luxi’); both actors rock massive sun- and moon-shaped headpieces.

Yes, the whole thing is just as bizarre as it sounds, but Qiu’s relentless visual brio keeps the soufflé aloft while the serious intent adds a complex, umami aftertaste with a hint of the tingly, numbing flavor so distinctive in Sichuan cuisine.

Indeed, much of the dialogue here is reportedly in the Sichuan dialect, a nuance that native speakers are likely to appreciate more than the international viewers, who may have caught this at the Tokyo Film Festival, where it premiered in competition. Nevertheless, the performances and the English-language subtitles succeed in getting across the mix of high and low cultures on display here, as each chapter throws together peasants and aristocrats, ordinary folk and fantastic beings, actors and filmmakers in a giddy muddle. The effect is a little reminiscent of commedia dell’arte with all that breaking-of-the-fourth-wall stuff, especially since the mise en scene here is so archly theatrical.

entertainment.title: Inside Jacksonville’s Historic — And Haunted? — Florida Theatre, Which Turns 100 Next Year
entertainment.summary: The nearly century-old venue has hosted acts including Elvis Presley, Fleetwood Mac and Bon Jovi — and according to some, it’s home to multiple active spirits.
entertainment.body:
In the summer of 2020, the historic Florida Theatre in Jacksonville, Fla., used the COVID-induced halt in touring to take care of some much-needed renovations. The former movie palace — which is now owned by the City of Jacksonville and the non-profit Florida Theatre Performing Arts Center — underwent capital improvements including new lighting, sound and video systems, as well as new seats — save for a pair in the balcony that were restored rather than replaced in honor of the theater’s ghostly friend, “J.”

According to multiple employees who spoke with Billboard , the grand, 1,900-seat movie palace — which took over a corner of Forsyth and Newman Streets that was formerly the site of a police station and jail — has hosted several paranormal specialists who claim to have witnessed ghostly activity in Section 500, Row E, Seat 2. This includes a figure seen sitting in the seat on video and sightings of what several have called an orb hovering over it. The alleged ghost haunting this spot got its name after a psychic consultant to a WJCT Public Television production said the apparition called himself J (either for Jay or Joy, an emotion the psychic said J felt for the theater). The psychic also noted that J was there to protect rather than harm.

“A lot of times when I’m in the theater, there’s only one seat that’s ever up, and it’s always the ghost seat,” says the theater’s marketing director Sarah Kraynik .

“There’s not a big sign [that] says ‘Ghost’ or ‘Beware of Ghost.’ It’s just, if you know, you know,” says Florida Theatre president Kevin Stone .

While the chairs look like all the others in the building, the theater gets calls from people throughout the year specifically asking to book the ghost seats, Stone says. The theater even sells a bumper sticker that reads, “I sat with the ghosts at the Florida Theatre.”

“There’s a little bit of a premium to those chairs,” says Stone. “It doesn’t hurt that the ghost seat is in the first row of the middle balcony, so there’s nobody in front of you.”

J may not be the only presence hanging around the ornate Mediterranean Revival building. Stone says construction workers have reported paint cans flying through the air and that multiple people have heard an electrical hum coming from unplugged items. Other strange occurrences, he says, include doors closing on their own and reports from theater staff of an unknown figure appearing in the projection booth.

What used to be a staple of pop music — the rapper/pop star collaboration — is basically dead. However, Lil Baby is willing to do his part to have the sector be revitalized.

Baby sat down with The New York Times’ Popcast on Thursday for an extensive conversation, which spilled into his aspirations to try stepping outside of his comfort zone for a glossy collaboration with a pop star like Sabrina Carpenter.

Pop star/rapper collaborations have become a rarity. Camila Cabello has been attempting to keep the crossover team-ups alive. The former Fifth Harmony singer recruited Drake for “Hot Uptown” and “Uuugly,” while also joining forces with Playboi Carti for “I Luv It” (No. 81 Billboard Hot 100 peak). All three were released in 2024 and landed on her C,XOXO album, which debuted at No. 13 on the Billboard 200.

Dua Lipa enlisted DaBaby for the dynamic “Levitating” remix in 2020, which dominated commercially, reaching No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2021.

Sabrina Carpenter does actually have a rap collab under her belt, clashing with Saweetie for “I Can’t Stop Me,” which landed on SC’s Singular Act II project in 2019.
